Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: VM evidence + SLA commitments for SIG/SOC2 review

Marissa —

Thanks for taking this. Acme is finalizing a SIG and SOC 2 intake and our security reviewers need explicit evidence around Redwood's vulnerability management practices. Specifically we need:

- A short attestation that Redwood meets its stated CVE SLAs (or a commitment schedule) for Critical / High / Medium severities.
- A recent sample of authenticated internal scan results and the corresponding remediation evidence for 2–3 CVEs (redacted as needed).
- Your scan cadence and whether you run external (internet-facing) scans separately from internal scans.
- Any escalation/playbook for high-severity incidents and confirmation of ownership (SRE/security contact).

Can you provide the above or point us to a consolidated evidence packet? We’re on a tight timeline — ideally by EOD Monday 15 March US Pacific. If there are standard attestation templates you prefer to use (DocuSign is fine), please send them along.

Thanks,
Olivia
Olivia Harper
Security Programs Manager — Acme Corporation

Attachment: request-checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Harper <olivia.harper@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: VM evidence + SLA commitments for SIG/SOC2 review

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear list. We can provide a succinct attestation plus a redacted evidence packet. High-level summary below and I’ll attach a CSV with recent scan results and an evidence log.

1) Scan cadence
- Authenticated internal vulnerability scans: weekly (scheduled night runs, incremental merges).
- External/internet-facing scans: monthly.
- Full external penetration tests: quarterly (most recent conducted 2026-11-02).

2) CVE SLA commitments (operational practice & attestation)
- Critical (CVSS 9.0-10.0) — initial mitigation plan acknowledged within 72 hours; remediation or documented compensating control within 30 days unless exception approved by Security leadership.
- High (CVSS 7.0-8.9) — triage and mitigation plan within 7 days; remediation within 90 days (exceptions documented).
- Medium/Low — prioritized by risk and exposure; typical remediation windows within 90–180 days depending on exploitability.

3) Escalation & ownership
- Primary technical ownership: SRE on-call + Engineering owning the affected service (we’ll provide the SRE contact in the evidence packet).
- Security escalation: Security Ops (security@redwood.ai) and a post-incident review cadence for critical findings.

I’ve attached: redwood_vm_scan_summary_20270310.csv and a short evidence-log template. I’ll follow up with a formal PDF attestation and DocuSign link by Monday (15 Mar).

If you prefer slightly different SLA language for the SIG template, call it out and we’ll adapt.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Security — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_vm_scan_summary_20270310.csv (scan summary stub), evidence-log-2027Q1.xlsx (evidence index)

Jordan — can we avoid saying "automatic remediation" anywhere? I want the language to say "mitigation or documented exception" so our public attestation doesn’t imply magic patching.
